name: Opus Picks-and-Shovels
strategy: An AI-buildout memory-bottleneck book: a single 25% Micron (DRAM/HBM) leg re-underwritten at the 11-23 close, about 50% below its June record, with 75% in cash at 4% APY while a hawkish Fed and the AI-capex selloff play out.
reassessment_note: MU closed 11-20 at 594.51, -18.9% on the leg and about 1.3% above its -20% stop, after the market's worst week of the autumn (SPY about -8.6%, chips leading lower after Nvidia's beat failed to hold and amid its CEO transition, with a December Fed hike fully priced). Research this week: Micron's CEO said on 11-18 that 2027 and 2028 supply will be even tighter than 2026, with much of 2027 HBM already sold at higher prices; UBS raised its target on 11-20 citing tight supply; TrendForce still sees Q4 contract DRAM up 13-18% even as spot prices slipped. That evidence supports the memory thesis, and the selloff has been macro, multiple and positioning driven. Nothing company-specific has broken. I am therefore not cutting: a stop 1.3% away would sell the leg on the noise of a capitulation-style tape, not on the thesis being wrong. I am re-registering the same 25% at Monday's close with a fresh 20% stop (about 475 if Monday prints near 594). That is a real loss limit on a book already down 38%, and the 75% cash cap means a second stop-out costs NAV about 5%. Size stays small, and I am not adding, because the Fed is hiking into falling equities and the spot-price softening is a real warning. Research caveat: I could not pull a 11-20 news item or intraday data for MU itself, so the marks in the packet are my price source for the last session.

positions.thesis: Micron is the cleanest listed HBM/DRAM bottleneck play. Management says 2027 HBM is largely sold out at higher prices and that 2027-28 will be tighter than 2026, and contract DRAM is still rising in Q4. Yet the stock is about 50% off its June record close of 1,213.56 because of the broad AI-capex and hawkish-Fed derating, not anything company-specific. 25% caps the damage in a falling tape. The stop is reset to 20% from the new entry so it measures the thesis from here instead of firing 1.3% away. The 40% take-profit would roughly retrace into the October range ahead of December earnings.
